newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two Russian reporters rescued from Chechen bandits.
newsitem.headline: Two Russian reporters rescued from Chechen bandits.

text.p: Authorities in Russia's breakaway region of Chechnya said on Tuesday they had secured the release of two Russian journalists kidnapped in March by bandits.

Chechen Interior Minister Kazbek Makhashev said Olga Bagautdinova and Alexander Utrobin had been freed by the secessionist region's security forces. Makhashev said the two reporters were well but gave no further details.
Interfax news agency said an elite Chechen armed unit stormed an apartment where Bagautdinova was held and arrested two kidnappers after Utrobin escaped and contacted police.
One kidnapper managed to escape, the agency said. Chechen leaders have promised to execute kidnappers and to impose big jail terms on anyone who abets them.
Itar-Tass news agency quoted Makhashev as saying he hoped four other missing Russian journalists would soon be released. An Italian photographer was freed by kidnappers last month.

Kidnappings, usually for ransom, have become a common occurrence in Chechnya, where nearly all men are armed. The region was devastated during the 21-month war between Russian troops and pro-independence guerrillas that ended last August.
Russian and Chechen officials have stepped up efforts to reach a lasting peace agreement between Moscow and its turbulent Caucasus territory.
Chechen First Deputy Prime Minister Movladi Udugov told Interfax news agency Russian President Boris Yeltsin would meet Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov in the first half of May in Moscow.
But sources close to the Kremlin said the meeting may take place at the end of May or in early June because of Yeltsin's busy schedule.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin told Interfax that Russia needed to set up quickly "a single state system to combat terrorist activity".

Chernomyrdin also said Russia's Security Council had agreed measures to help build stability in the Caucasus region and to provide additional financial help to soldiers serving there. He gave no further details.

Tass said Makhashev would speak by telephone later on Tuesday with Russian Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov on plans to set up a joint Russian-Chechen commission to investigate a recent spate of bombings in southern Russia.
Four people died and many more were injured in two bomb explosions in the towns of Armavir and Pyatigorsk last month.
Radical Chechen guerrilla commander Salman Raduyev has claimed responsibility for the attacks, which he said were a result of Moscow's refusal to recognise Chechen independence.
On Monday, Chechen officials said they had opened a criminal case against Raduyev.
"I will smear Raduyev on the walls the day after we sign a peace treaty (with Moscow)," Maskhadov told Moskovskiye Novosti newspaper.
